summary: The note surveys labor market policies and employment generation strategies in the post-pandemic period, covering skills development, social security, gig economy regulation, fiscal incentives, infrastructure investment and entrepreneurship support. It cites dated announcements and commentary from named officials and analysts between October 2023 and April 2024. It concludes that agile, collaborative policymaking is needed to build resilient labor markets.
one_line: Overview of post-pandemic labor market policies, from skills training and social security to gig work, tax incentives, infrastructure and startup grants.
key_facts: The International Labor Organization reported that the COVID-19 crisis wiped out 255 million full-time jobs in 2020 alone.
On October 5, 2023, Dr. Helen Zheng, Chief Economist at the Economic Strategy Institute, released statistics showing a recovery trend with disparities and challenges.
On November 13, 2023, Minister of Labor Adrian Klimt announced a comprehensive National Skills Strategy targeting youth and the existing workforce.
The National Skills Strategy combines vocational training, digital literacy programs, partnerships with educational institutions and industry, and apprenticeships and on-the-job training.

In an analysis published December 20, 2023, labor market analyst Susan Rawley argued that unemployment insurance, health benefits and retirement plans reduce workers' reluctance to leave unproductive jobs.
Portable benefits, which stay with workers as they move between jobs, are increasingly incorporated into labor market policies.
On January 15, 2024, labor advocates led by Jonathon Miles of the Workers' Rights Initiative convened to discuss regulating gig economy platforms for fair pay and labor standards.
Gig worker policies drafted afterward include minimum earnings thresholds, platforms for collective bargaining and dispute resolution mechanisms.
On February 10, 2024, economist Ava Chen spoke at an economic forum about targeted tax breaks for large firms and SMEs, and incentivizing industries with high employment multipliers.

As of March 2024, several countries launched infrastructure reforms to create millions of jobs in construction and engineering, emphasizing renewable energy, sustainable transport and green urban planning.
The 'Entrepreneur First' grant scheme was introduced on April 2, 2024, by the Small Business Association (SBA), providing startups with capital, mentoring and a streamlined regulatory environment.
Early pandemic-era measures included upskilling and reskilling programs, support for the gig economy and flexible work arrangements.
